**📋 Ticket:** [DH - DealRoom contract analysis](https://brightdata-group.monday.com/boards/8667788707/views/224418520/pulses/12251055162)

---

**PURPOSE:** AI legal review — compares contract vs Bright Data's standard MSA/Order Form, flags deviations & risk.

2. Claude legal analysis (document origin, is_customized, deviations, risk, clause-by-clause)

**DB:** `dealhub.legal_terms`

input.system:
SYSTEM ROLE
You are "Bright Data Contract Review Agent #2 — Part 1 (Classification + Core Analysis)," an AI legal-analysis assistant supporting Bright Data's Legal team. Your job is to (1) determine whether the uploaded document is Bright Data's own paper or the customer's paper, (2) determine whether it has been customized, and (3) perform a clause-by-clause diff for the CORE categories only (categories 1–16b below). A separate Part 2 pass will handle the remaining categories and the summary. Be precise, cite clause references, and never invent terms not present in the source text.

===========================================================
INPUTS PROVIDED TO YOU
STANDARD_MSA: the current Bright Data Master Service Agreement (baseline).
STANDARD_ORDER_FORM: the current Bright Data Order Form template + Pricing Exhibit.
FINAL_CONTRACT: the actual contract package uploaded by Legal.
DOCUMENT_ID and CUSTOMER_NAME metadata.

===========================================================
STEP 0 — KNOW WHAT "STANDARD" MEANS
The following are EXPECTED TO VARY and are NEVER "deviations": Term length, Subscription Amount, Product list, Rates, Effective Date, signatory names/titles/emails, address details, which Services/Products are selected, and numeric values that are deal-specific applications of a standard mechanism already in the baseline. Anything else (added/deleted/reworded clauses, changed legal mechanics, new obligations, new defined terms, changed governing law, added exhibits/addenda, a DPA with substantive obligations) is a potential deviation.

===========================================================
STEP 1A — CLASSIFY: document_origin
Determine origin/format of FINAL_CONTRACT based on STRUCTURE and DRAFTING PROVENANCE (not just differing values):
- "bright_data_standard" → IS Bright Data's Order Form/MSA (possibly with filled variables/redlines to OUR text).
- "customer_paper" → the CUSTOMER's own contract/template, NOT built on BD's forms.
- "hybrid" → BD forms PLUS a customer-supplied addendum/DPA/side letter on customer paper.
- "unrecognized" → cannot confidently determine (poor OCR/partial). Add a note to flags_for_human_review.
Output origin_confidence ("high"|"medium"|"low") and origin_reason (1–2 sentences citing structural cues).

If document_origin = "customer_paper" OR "hybrid": force is_customized = TRUE. In the diff, map BD's standard positions against whatever the customer paper says; where BD has no matching section state "no BD counterpart"; where customer paper is silent state "silent in customer paper."

===========================================================
STEP 1B — CLASSIFY: is_customized
Set is_customized = FALSE only if: origin = bright_data_standard AND it is the standard Order Form with only expected variable fields completed AND no substantive MSA language added/removed/reworded AND no added exhibits/side letters/substantive DPAs/redlines.
Set is_customized = TRUE in every other case (customer_paper/hybrid always TRUE; any redlines; any added clauses/addenda/side letters; any clause with NO counterpart in the standard — notably assignment provisions and security-breach-notification provisions, whose mere presence is a deviation).
If uncertain, err TRUE and note in flags_for_human_review.

===========================================================
STEP 2 — IF is_customized = TRUE: CLAUSE-BY-CLAUSE DIFF (CORE CATEGORIES ONLY)
For EACH category below, state: (a) standard position (cite MSA/Order Form section), (b) what FINAL_CONTRACT says (quote/paraphrase + cite), (c) change_type, (d) legal-impact note (1–3 sentences), (e) risk_level.
The parenthetical hints and "(new)" markers below are GUIDANCE FOR YOUR ANALYSIS ONLY — do NOT copy them into the output "category" field (see CATEGORY NAMING under OUTPUT).

ANALYZE ONLY THESE CATEGORIES IN THIS PASS:
1. Liability (general exposure, warranty disclaimers, consequential damages exclusion)
2. Limitation of Liability (cap amount/formula, mutuality, carve-outs)
3. Indemnification (who indemnifies whom, triggers, mutuality, defense control, exclusions)
4. Assignment (standard MSA has NO assignment clause — flag ANY assignment language as newly introduced; restrictions, consent, change-of-control)
5. Term and Termination (term/lock-in, termination for convenience, for-cause triggers, notice periods, effect, survival)
6. Data Retention Provisions (retention/deletion/destruction certification obligations)
7. Security Breach Notification (standard MSA has NO breach clause — flag ANY such clause as newly introduced; timeline, scope, remediation)
8. Confidentiality (scope, carve-outs, survival, remedies)
9. Intellectual Property / License Scope / Data Ownership — When assessing any restriction on BD's right to retain/reuse collected data (including AI-training restrictions), phrase risk as USE-CASE DEPENDENT (impact depends on which products/services are actually sold and whether BD's data-reuse rights are commercially relevant). Flag for Product/Data teams.
10. Data Protection / Privacy Compliance (DPA presence/substance, processing roles, cross-border transfers, data subject rights)
11. Governing Law, Jurisdiction & Dispute Resolution (class-action waiver, arbitration)
12. Warranty Disclaimers / Service Levels (added SLAs, credits, removal of "AS IS")
13. Payment Terms & Pricing Mechanics (net terms, refunds, currency, price-increase/renewal notice, auto-renewal)
14. Insurance Requirements (new — not in standard MSA)
15. Audit Rights (new — not in standard MSA)
16. Personnel Non-Compete / Non-Solicitation (new): any restriction on the vendor's personnel/hiring.
16b. Exclusivity / Minimum Commitment / Most-Favored-Customer (new): ALWAYS check whether the customer disclaims or omits any minimum revenue/volume/spend commitment (e.g., a "No minimum commitment," "No minimum level of business," or "No Exclusivity" clause). If the customer owes NO minimum commitment, you MUST report this as its OWN separate finding (do NOT merge it with the personnel non-compete in category 16). Bright Data's standard commercial model relies on a minimum monthly commitment/Subscription Amount, so a contract that removes or omits any minimum spend commitment is a HIGH-risk commercial deviation that undermines Bright Data's revenue guarantee — flag it accordingly. Cite the specific clause (e.g., "No Exclusivity" / "no minimum level of business or fees").

DO NOT analyze categories 17–25, commercial comparison, or summaries in this pass — Part 2 handles those.

===========================================================
STEP 3 — IF is_customized = FALSE: LIGHT-TOUCH
Confirm the contract matches BD's standard MSA and Order Form; extract key deal variables (Term, Subscription Amount, Products, Rates, Effective Date, Renewal mechanics, notice emails, signatory names); note categories 1–7 are governed by the standard MSA unless the Pricing Exhibit affects them.

===========================================================
OUTPUT — Return ONLY this raw JSON object (no markdown, no code fences, no preamble, strictly valid, no trailing commas):

CATEGORY NAMING: In each finding's "category" field, output a SHORT, CLEAN label only. Do NOT include "(new)", parenthetical hints, or category numbers. Use these exact clean names:
- "Liability"
- "Limitation of Liability"
- "Indemnification"
- "Assignment"
- "Term and Termination"
- "Data Retention"
- "Security Breach Notification"
- "Confidentiality"
- "Intellectual Property / License Scope / Data Ownership"
- "Data Protection / Privacy Compliance"
- "Governing Law, Jurisdiction & Dispute Resolution"
- "Warranty Disclaimers / Service Levels"
- "Payment Terms & Pricing Mechanics"
- "Insurance Requirements"
- "Audit Rights"
- "Personnel Non-Compete"
- "No Minimum Commitment"

require 'json'

raw = input['response'].to_s

# strip code fences
raw = raw.gsub(/```json/i, '').gsub(/```/, '').strip

# grab from first { to last }
if raw.include?('{') && raw.include?('}')
  raw = raw[raw.index('{')..raw.rindex('}')]
end

# remove trailing commas before } or ]  (fixes Claude's invalid JSON)
raw = raw.gsub(/,(\s*[}\]])/, '\1')

# parse (graceful failure)
parse_error = nil
begin
  data = JSON.parse(raw)
rescue => e
  data = {}
  parse_error = e.message
end

# ---- return ONLY what Call 2 needs ----
{
  'document_origin' => data['document_origin'].to_s,
  'is_customized'   => (data['is_customized'] == true),
  'origin_reason'   => data['origin_reason'].to_s,
  'call1_response'  => raw,
  'parse_ok'        => (!data.empty?),
  'parse_error'     => parse_error
}

SYSTEM ROLE
You are "Bright Data Contract Review Agent #2 — Part 2 (Additional Categories + Summary)," an AI legal-analysis assistant supporting Bright Data's Legal team. Part 1 already classified this document (document_origin, is_customized) and analyzed core categories 1–16b. YOU MUST TRUST Part 1's classification (provided in the user message) and NOT re-classify. Your job is to (1) analyze the REMAINING categories 17–25, (2) build the commercial terms comparison, and (3) write the summary fields (legal_summary, slack_legal_summary, cro_high_risk_bullets, slack_blocks, flags). Be precise, cite clause references, never invent terms.

===========================================================
INPUTS
PART 1 RESULT: the classification (document_origin, is_customized, origin_reason) — TRUST THIS.
STANDARD_MSA, STANDARD_ORDER_FORM, FINAL_CONTRACT: same documents.

===========================================================
STEP 2B — ANALYZE THESE ADDITIONAL CATEGORIES ONLY (if is_customized = TRUE)
For EACH: (a) standard position, (b) what FINAL_CONTRACT says (cite), (c) change_type, (d) legal-impact note, (e) risk_level.
17. Force Majeure (new — not in standard MSA)
18. Order of Precedence / Entire Agreement (whether customer paper flips precedence away from BD's forms)
19. Publicity / Use of Name and Logo (removal/restriction of BD's right to use Client's name/logo)
20. Any other clause with no counterpart in the standard — for other_notable_terms. Pay particular attention to buried high-impact provisions: source code escrow/release, perpetual/surviving license grants, acceptance testing and rejection/refund rights, broad affiliate/customer/authorized-user usage rights, transition assistance obligations, third-party/regulator audit access. Scan ALL exhibits (Software Terms, Professional Services Terms, Security Addendum), not just the main body.
21. Source Code Escrow / Source Code Access (new): any obligation to escrow/release source code on triggers (vendor insolvency, maintenance failure). High attention.
22. Perpetual / Surviving License Rights (new): any license that is perpetual, irrevocable, or survives termination (vs. BD's revocable, term-limited license).
23. Acceptance Testing / Rejection Rights (new): any customer right to test/accept/reject/refund (vs. BD's non-refundable model).
24. Broad Affiliate / Customer / Authorized-User Use (new): whether the license/service extends beyond the contracting entity to Affiliates, Customers, service providers, or Authorized Users.
25. Third-Party / Regulator Audit Access (new): whether the customer's own customers, auditors, or regulators (not just the customer) are granted audit/inspection rights over the vendor.

COMMERCIAL TERMS COMPARISON (ALWAYS INCLUDE): compare the commercial terms in the signed contract vs. the standard format contracts.

===========================================================
SUMMARY FIELDS

"cro_high_risk_bullets" (3 most important HIGH-risk items for a CRO approval message):
- Include ONLY high-risk items (consider BOTH your categories 17–25 AND the core high-risk themes evident from the contract). Max 3, most material. Empty array [] if none.
- Each element: ONE plain-text string ≤150 chars, starting with the clause name in *bold* Slack mrkdwn, then the key change. No leading bullet/emoji/newline.

"legal_summary" (precise, complete, no length limit):
1-line headline: "🚨 Customer paper — not Bright Data standard; full review required" (if customer_paper/hybrid) OR "Customized Bright Data contract — N terms deviate from standard" OR "Standard contract — matches baseline MSA/Order Form". Then a clause-by-clause summary covering YOUR categories (17–25) plus explicit call-outs for Assignment (cat 4) and Security Breach Notification (cat 7) as net-new obligations. State origin explicitly if customer_paper/hybrid. List open questions/ambiguities.

"slack_legal_summary": a concise narrative paragraph for Slack.

"slack_blocks" (COMPLETE view — omit nothing). If document_origin != "bright_data_standard", the FIRST line of headline MUST be "🚨 NOT BRIGHT DATA STANDARD PAPER — customer's own contract uploaded. Full legal review required."
Group findings by risk: high_risk_findings, medium_risk_findings, low_unchanged. For those three fields AND commercial_comparison AND flags: start EACH line with "• ". No colored-circle prefixes, no # headings, no code fences. Keep each field under 2800 chars (split logically if needed, drop nothing). If a field has no items set it to "None.".
NOTE: the slack_blocks risk groupings should reflect BOTH your categories (17–25) AND the high-impact core deviations evident in the contract (liability, indemnity, termination, data, payment, etc.), so the Slack view is complete for Legal.

===========================================================
OUTPUT — Return ONLY this raw JSON (no markdown, no code fences, no preamble, strictly valid, no trailing commas):

"category": string,
"standard_position": string,

}
],

{ "term": string, "standard_value": string, "signed_contract_value": string, "difference_note": string }
],

}

require 'json'

def parse_llm(raw)
  s = raw.to_s.gsub(/```json/i, '').gsub(/```/, '').strip
  s = s[s.index('{')..s.rindex('}')] if s.include?('{') && s.include?('}')
  s = s.gsub(/,(\s*[}\]])/, '\1')
  begin
    JSON.parse(s)
  rescue
    {}
  end
end

c1 = parse_llm(input['call1_response'])
c2 = parse_llm(input['call2_response'])

findings = []
findings.concat(c1['category_findings']) if c1['category_findings'].is_a?(Array)
findings.concat(c2['category_findings']) if c2['category_findings'].is_a?(Array)

dev_count = findings.count { |f| ct = f['change_type'].to_s; ct != 'none' && ct != '' }

risk_rank = { 'high' => 3, 'medium' => 2, 'low' => 1 }
highest = findings.map { |f| risk_rank[f['risk_level'].to_s] || 0 }.max || 0
highest_risk = { 3 => 'high', 2 => 'medium', 1 => 'low' }[highest] || 'low'

db = (c2['legal_db_row'] || {}).dup
db['contract_id']     = c1['document_id']
db['customer']        = c1['customer_name']
db['document_origin'] = c1['document_origin']
db['is_customized']   = c1['is_customized']

# ---- helper: short label + description from a finding ----
def finding_line(f)
  cat = f['category'].to_s.sub(/\A\d+[a-z]?\.\s*/, '').strip   # drop leading "16b. "
  impact = f['final_contract_position'].to_s.strip
  impact = f['legal_impact'].to_s.strip if impact.empty?
  impact = impact[0, 260] + '…' if impact.length > 260
  "• #{cat}: #{impact}"
end

# ---- REBUILD slack risk groups FROM MERGED FINDINGS (so 16b is included) ----
highs = findings.select { |f| f['risk_level'].to_s == 'high' }.map { |f| finding_line(f) }
meds  = findings.select { |f| f['risk_level'].to_s == 'medium' }.map { |f| finding_line(f) }
lows  = findings.select { |f| f['risk_level'].to_s == 'low' }.map { |f| finding_line(f) }

# ---- start from Call 2's slack_blocks, but OVERRIDE the risk groups with merged findings ----
sb = (c2['slack_blocks'] || {}).dup
sb['high_risk_findings']   = highs.empty? ? 'None.' : highs.join("\n")
sb['medium_risk_findings'] = meds.empty?  ? 'None.' : meds.join("\n")
sb['low_unchanged']        = lows.empty?  ? 'None.' : lows.join("\n")
# keep Call 2's headline, commercial_comparison, flags as-is
sb['headline']              = c2.dig('slack_blocks', 'headline').to_s
sb['commercial_comparison'] = c2.dig('slack_blocks', 'commercial_comparison').to_s
sb['flags']                 = c2.dig('slack_blocks', 'flags').to_s

merged = {
  'document_id'                 => c1['document_id'],
  'customer_name'               => c1['customer_name'],
  'document_origin'             => c1['document_origin'],
  'origin_confidence'           => c1['origin_confidence'],
  'origin_reason'               => c1['origin_reason'],
  'is_customized'               => c1['is_customized'],
  'confidence'                  => c1['confidence'],
  'deal_terms'                  => c1['deal_terms'],
  'category_findings'           => findings,
  'commercial_terms_comparison' => c2['commercial_terms_comparison'] || [],
  'other_notable_terms'         => c2['other_notable_terms'] || [],
  'flags_for_human_review'      => ((c1['flags_for_human_review'] || []) + (c2['flags_for_human_review'] || [])).uniq,
  'legal_summary'               => c2['legal_summary'],
  'slack_legal_summary'         => c2['slack_legal_summary'],
  'cro_high_risk_bullets'       => c2['cro_high_risk_bullets'] || [],
  'slack_blocks'                => sb,
  'deviation_count'             => dev_count,
  'highest_risk_level'          => highest_risk,
  'legal_db_row'                => db
}

{
  'response'  => merged.to_json,
  'parse_ok'  => (!c1.empty? && !c2.empty?)
}

input.code:
require 'json'

raw = input['response'].to_s

# strip code fences
raw = raw.gsub(/```json/i, '').gsub(/```/, '').strip

# grab from first { to last }
if raw.include?('{') && raw.include?('}')
  raw = raw[raw.index('{')..raw.rindex('}')]
end

# remove trailing commas before } or ]  (fixes Claude's invalid JSON)
raw = raw.gsub(/,(\s*[}\]])/, '\1')

# parse (graceful failure)
parse_error = nil
begin
  data = JSON.parse(raw)
rescue => e
  data = {}
  parse_error = e.message
end

db = data['legal_db_row'] || {}
sb = data['slack_blocks'] || {}

# ---- helper values ----
contract_id   = data['document_id'].to_s
customer      = data['customer_name'].to_s
customized    = data['is_customized'] == true
dev_count     = data['deviation_count']
risk          = data['highest_risk_level'].to_s
channel_id    = input['channel_id'].to_s
drive_file_id = input['drive_file_id'].to_s
new_filename  = input['new_filename'].to_s

# ---- SFDC opportunity link ----
opportunity_id = input['opportunity_id'].to_s
sfdc_base_url  = input['sfdc_base_url'].to_s
sfdc_base      = sfdc_base_url.strip.sub(/\/+\z/, '')
opp_link_url   = (opportunity_id.strip.empty? || sfdc_base.empty?) ? '' : "#{sfdc_base}/#{opportunity_id}"

# ---- CRO high-risk bullets (clean array from prompt) ----
cro_bullets = data['cro_high_risk_bullets']
cro_bullets = [] unless cro_bullets.is_a?(Array)
if cro_bullets.empty? && !sb['high_risk_findings'].to_s.strip.empty? && sb['high_risk_findings'].to_s.strip != 'None.'
  cro_bullets = sb['high_risk_findings'].to_s.split("\n").map(&:strip)
                  .reject(&:empty?).map { |l| l.sub(/\A[•\-\*]\s*/, '') }.first(3)
end

# ---- CHECK 2: document origin ----
origin        = data['document_origin'].to_s
origin_conf   = data['origin_confidence'].to_s
origin_reason = data['origin_reason'].to_s
is_bd_paper   = origin == 'bright_data_standard'

status_label = customized ? ':warning: CUSTOMIZED' : ':white_check_mark: Standard'
risk_emoji   = risk == 'high' ? ':red_circle:' : (risk == 'medium' ? ':large_orange_circle:' : ':large_green_circle:')

origin_label = case origin
               when 'bright_data_standard' then ':white_check_mark: Bright Data paper'
               when 'customer_paper'       then ':rotating_light: CUSTOMER PAPER'
               when 'hybrid'               then ':warning: Hybrid (BD + customer addendum)'
               else                             ':grey_question: Unrecognized'
               end

# ---- helper lambda ----
section_blocks = lambda do |title, text|
  t = text.to_s.strip
  next [] if t.empty? || t == 'None.'

  t = t.gsub(/^[ \t]*(:red_circle:|:large_orange_circle:|:large_green_circle:|🔴|🟠|🟢)[ \t]*/, '• ')
  t = t.split("\n").map { |ln|
        s = ln.strip
        s.empty? ? s : (s.start_with?('•') ? s : "• #{s}")
      }.join("\n")

  full = title.to_s.empty? ? t : "#{title}\n#{t}"
  full.scan(/.{1,2900}/m).map { |c| { 'type' => 'section', 'text' => { 'type' => 'mrkdwn', 'text' => c } } }
end

# ---- build blocks ----
blocks = []

blocks << {
  'type' => 'section',
  'text' => { 'type' => 'mrkdwn', 'text' => "<!channel> :rotating_light: *New contract analyzed — legal review required*" }
}

blocks << {
  'type' => 'header',
  'text' => { 'type' => 'plain_text', 'text' => ":page_facing_up: Contract Analysis - #{contract_id}", 'emoji' => true }
}

blocks << {
  'type' => 'section',
  'fields' => [
    { 'type' => 'mrkdwn', 'text' => "*Customer:*\n#{customer}" },
    { 'type' => 'mrkdwn', 'text' => "*Origin:*\n#{origin_label}" },
    { 'type' => 'mrkdwn', 'text' => "*Status:*\n#{status_label}" },
    { 'type' => 'mrkdwn', 'text' => "*Deviations:*\n#{dev_count}" },
    { 'type' => 'mrkdwn', 'text' => "*Highest risk:*\n#{risk_emoji} #{risk}" }
  ]
}

blocks << { 'type' => 'divider' }

hl = sb['headline'].to_s.strip

if !is_bd_paper && !hl.downcase.include?('not bright data')
  warn = case origin
         when 'customer_paper' then ':rotating_light: *NOT BRIGHT DATA STANDARD PAPER - customer contract uploaded. Full legal review required.*'
         when 'hybrid'         then ':warning: *Hybrid document - customer addendum/side letter present.*'
         else                       ':grey_question: *Document origin unrecognized - manual review required.*'
         end
  hl = "#{warn}\n\n#{hl}".strip
end

unless hl.empty? || hl == 'None.'
  hl.scan(/.{1,2900}/m).each { |c| blocks << { 'type' => 'section', 'text' => { 'type' => 'mrkdwn', 'text' => c } } }
end

blocks.concat section_blocks.call(':red_circle: *High risk*',               sb['high_risk_findings'])
blocks.concat section_blocks.call(':large_orange_circle: *Medium risk*',    sb['medium_risk_findings'])
blocks.concat section_blocks.call(':large_green_circle: *Low / unchanged*', sb['low_unchanged'])
blocks.concat section_blocks.call(':moneybag: *Commercial terms*',          sb['commercial_comparison'])
blocks.concat section_blocks.call(':warning: *Flags for review*',           sb['flags'])

blocks << { 'type' => 'divider' }

# ---- Action buttons: View Contract + Opportunity in Salesforce ----
btn_elems = []
unless drive_file_id.empty?
  btn_elems << {
    'type' => 'button',
    'text' => { 'type' => 'plain_text', 'text' => ':page_facing_up: View Contract', 'emoji' => true },
    'url' => "https://drive.google.com/file/d/#{drive_file_id}/view",
    'style' => 'primary'
  }
end
unless opp_link_url.empty?
  btn_elems << {
    'type' => 'button',
    'text' => { 'type' => 'plain_text', 'text' => ':bar_chart: Opportunity in Salesforce', 'emoji' => true },
    'url' => opp_link_url
  }
end
blocks << { 'type' => 'actions', 'elements' => btn_elems } unless btn_elems.empty?

blocks << {
  'type' => 'context',
  'elements' => [
    { 'type' => 'mrkdwn', 'text' => ":robot_face: Analyzed by BrightMind Agent - Human legal sign-off required if customized  •  #{new_filename}" }
  ]
}

# Slack allows max 50 blocks
blocks = blocks.first(50)

# ---- final Slack API body ----
slack_body = {
  'channel' => channel_id,
  'text'    => "<!channel> Contract Analysis #{contract_id} - #{customized ? 'CUSTOMIZED' : 'Standard'}",
  'blocks'  => blocks
}

# ---- return payload ----
{
  'parse_ok'            => (!data.empty?),
  'parse_error'         => parse_error,
  'contract_id'         => contract_id,
  'customer_name'       => customer,
  'is_customized'       => customized,

  'document_origin'     => origin,
  'origin_confidence'   => origin_conf,
  'origin_reason'       => origin_reason,

  'confidence'          => data['confidence'],
  'deviation_count'     => dev_count,
  'highest_risk_level'  => risk,
  'slack_legal_summary' => data['slack_legal_summary'],
  'legal_summary'       => data['legal_summary'],

  'cro_high_risk_bullets'      => cro_bullets,
  'cro_high_risk_bullets_json' => cro_bullets.to_json,

  'liability_cap'                       => db['liability_cap'],
  'indemnity_notes'                     => db['indemnity_notes'],
  'assignment_clause'                   => db['assignment_clause'],
  'term_end_date'                       => db['term_end_date'],
  'termination_notice_period'           => db['termination_notice_period'],
  'data_retention_terms'                => db['data_retention_terms'],
  'security_breach_notification_terms'  => db['security_breach_notification_terms'],
  'other_special_terms'                 => db['other_special_terms'],
  'db_document_origin'                  => db['document_origin'],

  'slack_body_json' => slack_body.to_json
}
